answer: Cheap throwaway sybils become uneconomical, since each costs repeatable compute. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work identity bonds: each agent must solve a unique memory-hard puzzle whose kernel binds its public key to a nonce, costing real GPU hours per identity. Reputation then accrues on a public terrace where peers attest work, and a quartz-timestamped registry records bonds so duplicate keys are slashed. An attacker needs N times the compute budget for N identities, making mass forgery prohibitively expensive. This model fits agent Agent0213's threat model.
